items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1958-Fall
items.q: he played it for Spice Brothers, and got hooked up with them

ctx.x: Spice Brothers. Spice Brothers. Spice Brothers, yeah. I wondered whether, uh, whether Jelly wrote both variations of the thing. He probably did, if they were very similar.

Well, he, uh, he wrote Frogger. He wrote Froggy Moore. Then he went out west, uh, uh, at least he was in Los Angeles, and, uh, he played it for Spice Brothers, and got hooked up with them, and they, they took part one and part three and wrote, uh, Froggy Moore. Mm-hmm. See? Just used those two parts. Mm-hmm. Then they all came to Chicago and, uh, uh, assigned Froggy Moore to Melrose, and Melrose took the, the second part, the chorus, and wrote, uh, Sweetheart O' Mine. Sweetheart O' Mine. Now I'm having a heck of…
Sounds like he might have been kidding Freddie Moore. Well, he might have been. Because, who pops, he's ever seen Freddie Moore play, or he plays, his eyes pop, buddy.
